components.name: Introduction to Business and Consumer Studies
Research Methods in the Social Sciences
Business and Consumer Perspectives on Food Quality
components.note: Examines food quality from business, consumer and food-science perspectives through lectures, assignments, a practical and a case. Required general and laboratory safety instruction carries no credits.

components.name: Quantitative and Qualitative Research Techniques in the Social Sciences
Food Innovation Research, a Gamma-Beta Approach
Financial Management in Agriculture
components.note: Selected restricted finance course: Financial Management in Agriculture. It develops farm financial management and accounting through qualitative and quantitative analysis. Corporate Financial Management is the other listed option.

components.name: Decision Science 2
components.note: Selected restricted methods course: Decision Science 2. It develops multi-criteria decisions, simulation, and decision analysis under risk. The handbook recommends it for a Business Economics or Operations Research thesis; the topic and methods choice must be agreed with the thesis coordinator.

components.name: Strategic Change Management and Innovation
components.note: Selected restricted strategy course: Strategic Change Management and Innovation. It applies organisational change and innovation theories to cases and stakeholder engagement. Supply Chain Design and Planning is the other listed option.

components.name: BSc Thesis Business Studies
components.note: The current handbook requires 102 credits of compulsory and restricted study, including all first-year courses. This 12 EC unit includes a one-credit Bachelor Assessment that must be passed before the 11 EC individual thesis. Research may be literature-based or empirical; a written report, presentation and oral defence are required. Current chair-specific preparation remains unverified.

components.name: Open Electives or Minor
components.note: Thirty EC remain open for a minor, an individual minor or elective courses.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both study managerial accounting, costs, budgeting and financial reports. WUR develops allocation, variances and transfer pricing in greater depth; UCR also teaches investment appraisal.
Both study contract and commercial interactions. UCR emphasises cross-border transactions; WUR includes domestic corporate, liability, competition and consumer law.
Both examine preferences, strategic interaction and economic models. WUR introduces a broader evidence-led economics approach; UCR develops more extensive microeconomic analysis.
Both develop customer needs, new products and value creation. UCR centres a product-design process; WUR combines these with broader management and marketing.
Both apply marketing and strategic analysis to firms and consumers. WUR additionally develops broader management strategy and implementation.
Both examine strategic change and innovation in organisations. UCR emphasises digital transformation; WUR uses broader organisational-change cases.
Both execute consumer research to inform product decisions. WUR integrates social and natural sciences in a commissioned food-product concept; UCR provides broader market research.
Both introduce businesses, consumer needs and practical inquiry. WUR centres sustainable agri-food chains and academic study; UCR develops a startup business plan.
Both develop feasible research questions and designs. UCR also conducts empirical research and introduces statistics; WUR centres a research proposal.
Both address utility, uncertainty and decision analysis. UCR includes Bayesian and sequential agent models; WUR also develops multi-criteria methods and simulation.
Both study constrained, linear and discrete optimisation. UCR frames these as intelligent-agent methods; WUR includes production and business decision models.
Both develop applied mathematical analysis with software. WUR also explicitly includes vector and matrix algebra; the UCR course does not supply that whole combination.
Both address probability, distributions and inference. UCR has a more extensive mathematical-statistics and sampling component.
Both develop qualitative research through evidence collection and analysis. WUR also includes quantitative techniques; this is partial correspondence.
Both examine social influence, attitudes and psychological accounts of behaviour. WUR integrates these with economics, sociology and marketing specifically for consumption.

notes.text: WUR integrates firms and consumers around food, products and value chains, with named Business and Consumer majors and compulsory individual research. UCR offers substantial business, consumer, data and sustainability study, but does not reproduce the dedicated food-quality, sensory-science, supply-chain and complete decision-science sequence. Optional UCR independent research is additional to the scheduled 180 credits.

audience.programmeDescription: Wageningen’s Business and Consumer Studies bachelor examines firms, consumers and the production and consumption of food and other products. This example follows the Business Studies major, with management, marketing, accounting, economics, research and quantitative decisions.
audience.comparisonExplanation: These UCR directions remain provisional while current thesis preparation for the Business Studies route is confirmed. The listed 180 EC credit framework is not a certified complete pathway.

curriculum.limitation: The listed components total 180 credits, but the current thesis guide’s remaining entry conditions have not been verified. This is a supported credit structure rather than a certified complete pathway.

componentNotes.y1-stat1: Introduces data collection, descriptive statistics, probability, distributions and hypothesis testing, with attention to good statistical practice.
componentNotes.y1-stat2: Develops statistical models, confidence intervals, tests of means, and simple regression and correlation, including interpretation and ethical practice.
componentNotes.y1-intro: Introduces sustainable agri-food chains, business and consumer perspectives, academic study and information literacy.
componentNotes.y1-management: Combines management and marketing, including business environments, strategy, customers, brands, products and value creation.
componentNotes.y1-sociology: Applies sociological concepts to businesses and consumption, including social change, institutions and globalisation.
componentNotes.y1-skills: Develops presentation delivery, self-awareness, observation and peer feedback through practice and personal learning goals.
componentNotes.y1-methods: Develops research questions, objectives and feasible proposals using experimental, cross-sectional and case-study designs.
componentNotes.y1-law: Introduces corporate, contract, liability, competition and consumer law, including relevant EU rules and basic legal reasoning.
componentNotes.y1-business: Introduces management accounting, financial management and financial accounting, with applications in agribusiness and food.
componentNotes.y1-food: Examines food quality from business, consumer and food-science perspectives through lectures, assignments, a practical and a case. Required general and laboratory safety instruction carries no credits.
componentNotes.y1-math: Develops applied mathematical analysis, vectors and matrices for social-science problems, supported by computer practicals.
componentNotes.y1-problem: A multidisciplinary group analyses a societal problem through a proposal, literature or interviews, ethical reflection and a written and oral report.
componentNotes.wur-MCB20806: Combines economic, sociological, psychological and marketing perspectives on consumption, consumer behaviour and social influence.
componentNotes.y2-decision1: Develops mathematical programming and constrained optimisation, including linear, integer and dynamic methods applied to practical decisions.
componentNotes.wur-DEC10306: Introduces evidence-led economic modelling, strategic interaction, information and preferences, using real-world problems and empirical research.
componentNotes.y2-research: Develops qualitative and quantitative data collection and analysis within the empirical research process.
componentNotes.y2-foodinnovation: Teams combine consumer research with social and natural sciences to develop a feasible food-product concept for a commissioning company.
componentNotes.y2-it: Examines the design and management of information and communication systems from organisational and consumer perspectives.
componentNotes.y2-management: Applies advanced management and marketing theory to strategy and implementation, building on introductory management and research methods.
componentNotes.y2-accounting: Develops cost allocation, budgeting, variance analysis, performance measurement and transfer pricing, with an introduction to financial reporting.
componentNotes.y3-agribusiness: Applies microeconomic and institutional theories to agribusiness, markets, contracts, food-production organisation, policies and trade.
componentNotes.y3-supply: Examines the coordination of supply-chain networks and flows of goods, services, money and information, using research and business cases.
